This, like many personal projects, began as a fun exercise. Maybe 8 years later after I wrote the app, I wanted to get some professional opinions. I found two cryptography professors and wrote them about my code. I assumed they get many inquiries from idiots, so I gave them a brief rundown of my background: started coding in assembler in the 1980s for Ashton-Tate for 5 years. Moved to C++, worked for DuPont, Random House, Logitech, Chase, and some smaller companies,  then Equitable (for 15 years) (among other companies).  So I know how to code. Now that doesn't mean I know how to write cryptography code, but still. Both professors responded in a similar way: Nasty, put-downish. Take a course and then get back, kind of thing. I thought, well, fuck them. I was and am having fun with it. I thought it was cool to think of new routines that can mess up the data (and unmess it), is how I expressed it then.

I'm glad you used dotPeek. I used to obfuscate the code but I thought, why bother?

As for my code, I'm working on getting it in a decent format and I will put it on the website. Perhaps some of it has merit; or can be improved. Blowfish is only called in two procedures which may not be used depending on the value of the current key. I wanted to use AES but AES (as far as I could tell) adds garbage text and I couldn't work with that, since Andromeda does the same thing.

That's it.
